title: Team AI training for nonprofits | Creosote Labs
meta_description: A one-day, hands-on AI workshop for nonprofit staff, taught on their own grant narratives, donor letters, and reports. $1,000 per person, 5-person minimum.
intro: Nonprofit staff tend to wear several hats, and most of them involve writing: a development director drafts appeals and grant narratives, a program manager writes funder reports and case notes, an executive director prepares board memos, and a communications coordinator produces the newsletter and social posts. Many organizations already have Google Gemini or Microsoft 365 Copilot through a nonprofit license and have not yet worked out how to apply it to those tasks.

Creosote Labs delivers a one-day, hands-on workshop on the organization's own tools and documents. Each participant works on their own computer with their own material, whether that is a pending grant application, a stack of thank-you letters, or the next board report, and leaves with a working setup and a process they documented themselves. The team receives a written guide, and a follow-up session 30 days later is part of the engagement.
projects: A development director drafts a year-end appeal, with versions for three donor segments, from last year's letter and the gift history.
A program manager turns a quarter of case notes into the outcomes section of a funder report.
An executive director builds a reusable prompt that produces a board memo from the month's financial statements.
A communications coordinator converts one program story into a newsletter article, two social posts, and a website update.
A grants manager sets up a reference file of past proposals so new applications start from approved language.

faqs.q: What does the training cost and how many people can attend?
faqs.a: The rate is $1,000 per person for up to 10 people, with a 5-person minimum. Larger teams are quoted, and travel is included. The version with three monthly follow-up sessions costs $1,400 per person.

faqs.q: Which AI tool is the workshop taught in?
faqs.a: The workshop is taught in whichever tool the organization already uses, such as Google Gemini, Microsoft 365 Copilot, or Claude. Participants leave with a setup in the tool they will actually open the next day.

Participants bring their own computer, access to the organization's documents, and 1 or 2 real tasks they need to complete that week. The day is spent producing that work, not watching demonstrations.
